chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Aban, from Abdul Malik who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the Fast of Tasua and Ashura from the month of Muharram, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'Tasua is a day in which Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) and his companions, may Allah be pleased with them, were surrounded in Karbala, and the cavalry of the people of Syria gathered against him and encamped upon him, and Ibn Marjana and Umar ibn Sa'd rejoiced at the abundance and multitude of the cavalry, and they considered Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) and his companions, may Allah be pleased with them, to be weak, and they were convinced that no helper would come to Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) nor would the people of Iraq support him, by my father, the oppressed, the alienated.'

Then he (peace be upon him) said: 'And as for the day of Ashura, it is a day in which Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) was killed as a corpse among his companions, and his companions were corpses around him, stripped. So, can a Fast be on that day? No! By the Lord of the Sacred House, it is not a day of Fasting, and it is not except a day of grief and calamity that entered upon the inhabitants of the sky and the inhabitants of the earth and all the believers.'

And it is a day of joy and happiness for Ibn Marjana and the progeny of Ziyad and the people of Syria. May Allah be Wrathful upon them and upon their offspring. And that is a day in which all the spots of the earth wept for him, except for the spot of Syria. So whoever fasts it or considers it fortunate, Allah will resurrect him with the progeny of Ziyad, morphed of the heart, Angered upon; and whoever hoards provisions in his house, Allah the Exalted will cause hypocrisy to be the end result in his heart until the day he meets Him, and He will snatch away the Blessing from him and from the people of his household and his children, and the Satan will be his partner in all of that.'

key_terms.ابْنُ مَرْجَانَةَ: Umar ibn Hubayra, known as Ibn Marjana, a Umayyad commander
key_terms.عُمَرُ بْنُ سَعْدٍ: Umar ibn Sa'd, the commander of the army at Karbala
key_terms.كَرْبَلَاءَ: Karbala, the site of the martyrdom of Imam Husayn
key_terms.مَمْسُوخُ الْقَلْبِ: Morphed of the heart, indicating a change in nature or state

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on fasting on the 9th and 10th of Muharram according to Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him)?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) distinguishes between Tasua, marked by the encirclement of Imam Husayn (AS), and Ashura, the day of his martyrdom, declaring the latter a day of profound grief rather than fasting. He provides a theological rationale for the Shia practice of fasting on Ashura by contrasting the mourning of the faithful with the joy of the Umayyad enemies, specifically Ibn Marjana and the people of Sham. The Imam warns that those who fast or celebrate this day share the spiritual fate of the Umayyads, suffering from hypocrisy and the removal of divine blessing.
